macrocycle.short: The longest unit of a training plan: usually a season or a year, built towards the main race or races.

mesocycle.short: A middle unit of a training plan, usually 2–6 weeks, with one main aim (for example building volume or race-pace work).

microcycle.short: A short unit of a training plan, usually one week, sometimes a few days.

traditional-periodisation.short: A season plan that starts with lots of easy volume and slowly swaps it for less volume and more intensity as the main race nears, training many abilities at once.

block-periodisation.short: Packing hard sessions into a short, concentrated block (for example five interval sessions in one week), then training lightly, instead of spreading them evenly.

reverse-periodisation.short: The mirror of traditional periodisation: hard, short, low-volume training first, with volume added closer to the race.

taper.short: The last days to weeks before a key race, when training is cut back so fatigue clears while fitness stays.

progressive-taper.short: A taper in which training volume falls a bit more each day or week, instead of all at once.

step-taper.short: A taper in which training volume is cut once, to a fixed lower level, and held there until the race.

functional-overreaching.short: A short, planned dip in performance after a hard block of training that turns into a gain once the athlete has recovered, within days to a couple of weeks.

supercompensation.short: Performance rising above its earlier level once you recover from a hard training period.

priority-race.short: A coach's way to rank races: A races are the season's targets you taper for, B races matter but get only a short easing, C races are trained through.

recovery-week.short: A planned lighter week, often every third or fourth week, to let fatigue clear before the next build. Common in practice, rarely tested.

transition-phase.short: The few weeks of easy, unstructured activity after the season's last race, to recover in body and mind before the next build.
